about: A guide to Snowmoon's world for planning pieces: characters, places, geography (where places are, each line also stated as one relation), institutions and technology, Minpentai, factions and a timeline. Every line cites the blocks it rests on and carries from_chapter, the latest chapter it depends on, so it can be filtered to how far someone has read.
label: AI-made: written by an AI model, Claude (the coding agent, a closed model), from the book and from the spoken summary's chapter notes; each line checked against its cited passages. Not by the author.
license: A guide to Snowmoon by Vitalik Buterin, made from the book on 2026-10-11. GPL-3.0, like the book.

lines.text: A Veridian citizen in Meldan and an Acolyte, an Order of Steering member in training.
Thirty-nine; from a fairly middle-class family; took up programming and law in his spare time.
To become a Sentinel; his prediction score is ninety-two, and above ninety he gets in.
Steering to reward openness: writing an alternative client for Silverchat's open interface is what drew him into Steering.
Being exposed: the Order's security rests on its members' privacy, and a bounty rewards anyone who guesses a member's task.
Chooses to apply as a Keeper rather than a Sentinel, after Delwart's push and Seila's encouragement.
Is accepted into the Order by a ten-to-ten committee vote broken by the chairman.
Goes to Dzego to learn how it resists the Arctics, and becomes a de facto adviser to the Kungaupei.
Apologizes to Seila for not trusting her mind as well as her heart.
Partner of Seila; father of Zven and Lily; "Uncle Glad" to Febric.
Close friend of Mov, who calls him Glad.
Gladias's partner, a Veridian blogger who writes about economics and culture.
Gladias to use the Keeper role to make the tax rules help Dzego.
Sees through Delwart's Silverchat story, tracks down other Keepers he approached, and concludes he is not from Silverchat.
Concludes Delwart is an Arctic propagandist working to make the Order ineffective.
Proposes a Silverchat poll to show the courts that changing the army would be democratic.
Friend of Jahn in Freetown; meets Zei and Bai there by chance.
Gladias's friend in the Order, who jokes that he is the Arctic Emperor.
To shadow Gladias at his meetings and find out who Delwart really is.
Is selected at random to become a Herald, a retired member with no formal power.
Follows Delwart for months; later searches for the truth with Seila.
A man in a privacy robe who tracks Gladias down and meets him in Greater Plum Harbor.
Says he wants "actual freedom": fewer nudges, and Keepers who delete every rubric.
After Redshire falls, claims he works with others for Silverchat.
Seila finds he told each Keeper something different, and concludes he is an Arctic.
Zei Leimin, a student in Pafogai Du and a Minpentai player.
To win the Minpentai championship, partly to buy his mother a compute box with the prize money.
That the Arctic threat is real, after his classroom is bombed and his arm broken.
Is recruited by Den into defense and switches his studies to cryptography.
Is named national champion when the final is cancelled, and says he does not want to win like this.
Supervises the drone battle for Northshore.
Close friend of Fin; rival, then ally and friend, of Bai; friend of Deluin.
His mother is Min.
Zei's friend in Pafogai Du, a student training with the Bansunpei.
Explains that Dzegoban is coordination training, and that the Bansunpei used its channels to change Dzego's habits after Redshire.
Helps build the attack on the Arctic drones' AI with Bansunpei researchers.
Bai Jahen, Zei's Minpentai rival in Pafogai Du.
Losing what she has: her parents died in a lab explosion, and all she had was her success.
Success as proof she is strong; she later says Zei's curiosity was a purer motive.
Learns to cooperate with Zei, then gives him advice and hugs as a friend.
Considers spending a year in Thaldur to understand the Arctics.
An older woman in Dzego who knows Zei, at the Minpentai games.
Explains that Minpentai is military training; later works with the Kungaupei.
Saves the rescue of Tafindel with a new plan, and takes over Group South when Den is lost.
A High Council member of the Kungaupei.
To recruit Zei into defense; after Redshire, for the shadow society to become the society.
Leads Group South in the battle for Northshore and is almost certainly killed when a rear base is hit.
A contestant from Redshire at Dzego's national championship.
Trapped by the invasion; his parents side with the Arctics, and he plays along to win their trust.
Becomes an Arctic commander and helps Veridia break the southern flank.
Befriends Zei at the nationals and invites him to Redshire.
Gladias and Seila's daughter, who struggles at school.
Is drawn to Arctic propaganda and runs away to Arctic-held Northglade.
Argues back at her Arctic teacher, is put in detention, and wants to come home.
Gladias and Seila's younger son.
Wins a Helisport game; stays in touch with Lily and learns where she is.
Teenage son of Vil and Daia, the co-family; studies computer science.
Daughter of Vil and Daia; good at mathematics.
With Hreda, takes refuge in Northglade's Greater Plum Harbor when Northshore is invaded.
Uncle Vil, co-parent with Aunt Daia; part of a class action by Jump's former employees against the hedge fund Divergent.
Seila's friend in Freetown, a researcher at the Freetown Economics Institute.
Introduces Zei to Freetown's defense companies through the Institute's director.
A Veridian senator who questioned Gladias at his hearing.
Proposes using the courts to replace the failed military leadership.
The Arctic ambassador to Veridia, who argues that only economic growth compounds.
President of Veridia National University, who debates Ephelion.
A respected Veridian general who becomes head general and commands the battle for Northshore.
The founder of Silverchat.
The son of Redshire's president, held by the Arctics and rescued by the Kungaupei.
Zei's mother; Freetown is her first trip abroad.
A Minpentai priest and an organizer of the nationals.
A country of trees and medieval-style stone houses; its capital is Meldan.
Veridia's capital, with the forest-like Kalimar district, sky bridges and a tree-covered mountain.
A walled enclave in Meldan, "almost like a country inside a country"; many Veridians push its land taxes up.
Its buildings are uniform, futuristic glass and steel, unlike the rest of Veridia.
A country that lost a war to the Arctics a century ago and grows its strength in small, spread-out workshops.
A Dzego city of small electronics shops and factories on a regular street grid.
A half-kilometer pyramid at its southern edge is a refurbished mountain holding part of the government.
Dzego's capital; the name means "main city".
Cities that elect a share of each other's parliaments, called co-governance.
A city of the United Cities, mixed rich and run-down, with the Freetown Economics Institute.
A country of castles, pine forests and red snowy mountains.
Invaded and annexed by the Arctic Empire.
A Veridian town in the province of Northshore, near the Arctic border, with Veridia's best math university.
Taken by the Arctics, except its Greater Plum Harbor, which they leave alone.
An island of the Arctic core territory east of Northshore, taken by Veridian sea drones.
An Arctic city like a giant ice crystal, with a kilometer-tall tower.
Snowy pine forest in Veridia where the battle for Northshore begins.
A government-linked, decentralized collective that sets Veridia's taxes and subsidies instead of bans.
Keepers vote on tax rubrics; Sentinels audit businesses; Acolytes are members in training.
Anyone can guess a member's task for a bounty, so members keep their roles private.
Each rubric has twenty-one Keepers in three groups of seven that discuss separately and don't know who is in the other groups; thirteen votes pass a change.
Order members picked at random to retire and explain the Order to the public, transparent only once they have no power.
Five judges per case, chosen at random from a large pool and anonymous; an appeal draws a new sample.
Public funding split down a graph, each node's share decided by a randomly selected committee.
Public matching of donations; attacked by Bluewhale and later at larger scale by the Arctics.
Veridia's transparent parliament; a committee of twenty senators approves new Order members.
Public meetings, some run by Heralds, whose results Keepers check when debating rubrics.
Dzego's Decentralized University, which runs by anonymous cryptographic coordination.
The priests who keep improving the Dzegoban language, testing versions across the country.
Dzego's secret society for defense, a shadow army.
The Veridian privacy robe: a loose dark purple garment covering the body from hood to ankles.
A band that picks up silent, whispered speech.
The local AI on Gladias's hand device.
Watches and gates verify devices and credentials while learning nothing else.
A common material lining rooms to block wireless signals.
Messages, and in Dzego even parcels, pass through three randomly chosen nodes so no one sees both sender and receiver.
In Dzego anyone may unscrew a public camera and inspect it, so cameras can be trusted.
The currency; payments and even sales tax are zero-knowledge.
A hundred ticks a minute, a hundred minutes a longhour, ten longhours a day.
Veridia's two big social platforms: Silverchat open to other clients, Bluewhale closed.
A drinks brand known for its odd, funny advertisements.
A strategy game played on a board of walls, gliders and ships carrying each player's symbol.
Its rules are time-reversible, so anything that can be built can be destroyed.
Each match has a new rule chosen by priests.
Intervention turns let players add squares near their symbols.
Really military training: a way to raise defenders, safe because it looks like a game.
Its players sit in Veridia's command centres and help run the drones in the battle for Northshore.
The most technologically advanced power; its aim is to keep Dzego's industry and technology down.
Its ideology rates people by intelligence and treats love as a reward for winning.
Smuggles surveillance devices into Veridia and corrupts officials.
Invades Redshire, then Northglade.
Its slogan, "grow roots, no head": spread-out manufacturing and anonymous coordination with no leaders to target.
"Dze go ba fau gie": Dzego will rise again.
Arm after Redshire, and later help Dzego hunt Arctic drones.
The more open social platform, which Delwart claims to work for.
Meldan: Gladias rates a band as an Acolyte, escapes being exposed, and gets an anonymous request.
Pafogai Du: a blast hits Zei and Fin's class; Zei's arm is broken.
Meldan: Gladias meets Delwart, who urges him to become a Keeper.
Pafogai Du: Zei and Bai win a quarter final together.
Freetown: Zei, Min and Bai meet Seila and Jahn.
Meldan: Gladias applies to become a Keeper.
Pafogai Du: a chip factory is hit; Bai resigns and Zei wins the city final.
Meldan: Gladias is accepted into the Order; Mov becomes a Herald.
Pafogai Du: Den recruits Zei into defense.
Freetown prepares; Gladias attends his first Keeper meetings; Zei learns Minpentai is military training.
Meldan: Zven wins at Helisport.
Sadzu Du: the national championship begins; Zei meets Deluin.
Meldan: Mov finds Delwart has contacts in two discussion groups of one rubric; Gladias's group agrees to wait two months.
Sadzu Du: Zei and Deluin win their semi finals.
The Arctic Empire invades and annexes Redshire; the final is cancelled.
Meldan: Delwart claims to work for Silverchat.
Meldan: the Keepers vote on the hardware openness rubric.
Pafogai Du: Gladias arrives in Dzego.
Pafogai Du: Deluin's letter reaches Zei.
The Arctic Empire invades Northglade; Seila finds Delwart is not from Silverchat.
Meldan: Seila concludes Delwart is an Arctic.
Freetown and Pafogai Du: drone hunts in Redshire; Lily runs away.
Pafogai Du: Gladias proposes that Dzego spy on Veridia's spies.
Pafogai Du: the plan to persuade Veridia's courts.
Veridia: Tafindel is rescued; the judges refuse the case.
Meldan: the Silverchat poll and the forecasting bots.
Meldan: Lektor becomes head general.
Elenar Forest: the battle for Northshore.
Northglade is retaken and Thaldur taken.
Northglade: Zei meets Deluin; Gladias's family is reunited.
Meldan: Verdow warns this was only the first round.
Learns that Minpentai is military training, and promises to tell no one, not even Fin.
Tells Deluin how to hide messages better in an Arctic soldier's health data; the soldier sends thanks.
Directs drone hunts in Redshire with Freetown's defense companies; Den calls him one of their best cryptographers.
Supervises the main plan of the rescue of Tafindel, and says he failed completely when Mu's new plan saves it.
Trusts Deluin's battlefield messages and passes his coordinates to Mu, opening the southern front.
Wants AI to be a player, not the game: Veridia's institutions, he says, have no built-in concept of predicting the future.
Is asked by Verdow to stay and help figure out the questions facing Veridia's government, and agrees.
Sends Zei a letter hidden in an obfuscated language model that asks him to describe their day together.
Suggests that Dzego backdoor the security cameras Veridia buys from Dzego; Verdow later credits him with it.
There are over a thousand Keepers; in a rubric circle they know each other only by numbers.
A Keeper's voting key is made by meeting at least three of five people in a Key Allocation Group, and no one can tell which keys are valid.
To be accepted, an Acolyte needs a prediction score in the top ten percent and a Senate committee's approval.
Delwart got contacts in two discussion groups of the same rubric, defeating the point of splitting them.
Mu calls Steering one of the most opaque parts of Veridia's government, and one of the most trustworthy for that reason.
Rubrics get gamed and then adjusted; one rewarding ground-floor active use is gamed with things nobody wants to use.
With the latest rubric changes, Silverchat's taxes have dropped to zero for its transparency, interoperability and privacy.
After the war, Verdow says the Order, the Courts and Graph Funding worked, and everything more transparent broke.
A small mountain stands in the center of Meldan; homes fill its lower half, and part of the government works in its upper half.
The business district lies east of the mountain.
Kalimar district lies south of the mountain; it looks like a forest but holds many hidden homes.
A large residential district lies west of the mountain.
Meldan has 1.1 million people and many districts.
Shortly before the aeroplane descends, the view is a mostly flat, green landscape; the Gelebor mountains, a row of small mountains, are on the right, and Meldan lies beyond them.
A footpath through Kalimar, between stone houses behind trees, gives way to shrubbery, curves upward and becomes a sky bridge over a busy road.
Cars can only go up to the border of a car-free zone in Kalimar; the last few hundred meters are on foot.
A right turn off the usual Kalimar path leads about a hundred meters, past stone houses and then forest, to a door into what looks like a small hill, where they meet Evelor.
Silverchat's headquarters is in Kalimar, visible from parliament's roof among the trees.
A few hundred meters along the forested path through Kalimar, a right turn and thirty meters lead to a stone house that is mostly underground.

From the middle of the sky bridge, turning to his left and looking along it, Gladias sees the busy road beneath run on about two kilometers and turn right; beyond that point is the tree-covered mountain, with castle-shaped apartment towers on its lower slope.

relation.rel: beyond the road's right turn, about two kilometers to the left of

lines.text: To the right of the sky bridge, the road runs on past much denser buildings. Past the bridge, five-storey apartments line the left side and a soundproof barrier the right.
Badra St #1103, a five-storey apartment building, is in view soon after the sky bridge, while Gladias walks beside the soundproof barrier; he thinks of the area as already a corporate district.
Standing by Badra St #1103 and looking at other nearby buildings, Gladias can just make out, in the distance, the building shaped like an aeroplane, an aviation company's headquarters.
A minute's walk further on, an opening in the soundproof barrier is the entrance to the concert; after it, a fifteen-minute autobus ride and a short walk take Gladias home.
Past the sky bridge, the path goes into a tunnel and reaches a Y-shaped intersection.

On a walk through Meldan that next finds him at Greater Plum Harbor's gate, Gladias crosses a street, goes down into a tunnel and passes a Y-shaped intersection with a poster from Lord Ephelion; the tunnel comes up among trees, then a more urban, commercial part of Meldan.
The Y past the sky bridge is the one with Lord Ephelion's poster: when Gladias next comes through, the poster is gone. He turns left there for what may be only the second time in his life.

relation.a: the Y of the Greater Plum Harbor walk
relation.b: the Y past the sky bridge

lines.text: Left at the Y, the path comes back above ground, snakes under highways, and becomes a straight, two-hundred-meter-tall outdoor staircase on the side of the mountain; about ten minutes of climbing, a tunnel and two flights of stairs lead to the top floor of the Order's tower.

relation.rel: at the top of a 200-meter staircase on

lines.text: Parliament, a large circular building, is about twenty minutes' walk from the Y: left at the Y, then right once the path is back above ground.

Parliament stands partway up the mountain, about forty meters above most of Meldan; looking out from its roof toward Kalimar, the mountain begins to rise properly about two hundred meters to the right.

From parliament's roof, looking toward Kalimar: the commercial district to the left, Greater Plum Harbor further left, Kalimar in front, and the mountain to the right. The concert venue is on the commercial district's right edge.
Meldan's Greater Plum Harbor is a square nearly a kilometer wide.

relation.b: a square nearly a kilometer wide

lines.text: Greater Plum Harbor is walled, with an entrance gate; inside, walking through its tunnels to the exit takes about ten minutes, and its doors open onto Meldan's commercial district.

Gladias's street is lined with similar recent houses; turning right from his door, he passes a house with a coffee shop within three hundred meters and reaches a community center at the first street corner.
Galanar Square is on the border of Kalimar, about a kilometer south of that community center, where the assembly is held.
Tapaia Square is about a kilometer further west than Galanar Square.
Soon after the assembly, Gladias eats at a restaurant; from there, a few hundred meters along the street and a right turn lead into forest, then the stone houses of Kalimar, then the sky bridge.

relation.b: a restaurant near the community center

lines.text: Pafogai Du is a perfectly regular grid: seventeen streets two hundred meters apart from north to south, and thirty-three streets one hundred meters apart from east to west.
Named streets are two hundred meters apart, and house numbers are meters: turning off at 20th street, Zei counts from 2000.
Mun Gui is four named streets from Hun Min. From 1990 Hun Min, Fin and Zei turn left on 20th street and left again on Mun Gui to reach 1842, about 958 meters.
0th street is on the west edge of the city.

relation.b: the west edge of Pafogai Du

lines.text: Dzai Gun is the last street before Pafogai Du ends in the south; a straight path to the pyramid's entrance begins there, and the hill begins after it.

relation.b: the south edge of Pafogai Du

lines.text: A half-kilometer-tall mountain pyramid stands at the southern edge of Pafogai Du.
Turning onto 17th street with the pyramid, which is south of the city, in front of him, Gladias crosses Zin Go and then Dzai Gun, where the pyramid path starts: two streets on.

relation.a: Tan Kai, Zin Go, Dzai Gun
relation.rel: in order from north to south

lines.text: Gladias's hotel is at 1565 Tan Kai. He turns right out of it, then right on 17th street, with the pyramid in front of him.
A tree-covered path runs around the whole perimeter of the city. Following it west along Dzai Gun, it turns north at 0th street; Tan Kai is two streets north of Dzai Gun.
On 17th street before Zin Go, shops and stairways down to basements come about twenty meters apart.
Pafogai Du is low-rise: one- and two-storey buildings, many stairways leading underground, and car lanes that go below ground where sidewalks need the space.
The street up to the pyramid curves up at about a ten percent slope; from somewhat further up, the whole grid is in view, and the main door is about five minutes on.

Two rows of trees line the path up to a point halfway to the top, and a row of trees runs around the pyramid at exactly half its height; from the main door, a horizontal tree-covered path leads thirty meters to a side entrance.
About five minutes up the incline from Dzai Gun, Gladias is high enough to see the roofs of nearly the whole city.

relation.a: a view over the city's roofs

lines.text: Living in the pyramid at the south end of Pafogai Du, Gladias took daily twenty-minute walks for over two months along the trees around its perimeter halfway up, and sometimes longer walks down into the nearby forest.
The pyramid is a pre-existing mountain with caves made into living and working space; a cafeteria inside is thirty meters below ground.
On the drive into Pafogai Du, a tunnel swaps cabins between cars; less than a minute after leaving it, the pyramid south of the city comes into view.
Sadzu Du, Dzego's capital, is reached from Pafogai Du by train.
In Sadzu Du, several mountain pyramids, each about half as tall as the one south of Pafogai Du, stand behind a park; past the park, a bridge crosses a small river.
Sadzu Du has a southern mountain pyramid, and the qualifying matches are in its "north stadium".
The Beautiful Plants food court is at 2415 Len Su street, Sadzu Du.
Zei, his mother Min and Bai arrive in Freetown through its air harbor; it is Min's first time abroad.
From Sadzu Du, Deluin flies home to Redshire.
Zei, Bai, Gladias and Den come to Meldan by aeroplane.
Seila calls Dzego halfway across the world from Veridia; in Pafogai Du, everyone Gladias could hug is thousands of kilometers away.
Speaking in Meldan, Gladias says Northglade is pretty far northeast, almost at the Arctic border.
Hreda says Northglade is not right at the border: it is over two hundred kilometers inland.
Seila, at home in Meldan, says Febric and Hreda are stuck a thousand kilometers away.
From Meldan, people speak of a trip "up to Northglade" and of being "up north" there, with months of snow and no green.
Northglade is in the province of Northshore, and a Greater Plum Harbor is inside Northglade.
The Arctics descended on Northshore from all sides.
Lily's Arctic boarding school in Northglade is about a kilometer from the Greater Plum Harbor.
Northglade is on an island about twenty kilometers wide, too small for the most simplified, zoomed-out maps of the region to show.
From the platform at the top of a mountain on the island, the main city of Northglade lies to the east; snowy hills and forest stretch west and north.
A Hydrafill advertisement says its Veridian northern ice is extracted thirty kilometers from the Arctic border.
From the forests where the army gathers, served by the last train to Eldil, the plan is to push into the northern part of Northshore from the west and bypass Northglade.
Group North crosses the forest and goes far northeast to the coast, cutting the Arctics off from the whole peninsula; Arctic reinforcements would come on its northern flank.
Group Center crosses the forest directly east.
Group South crosses the forest toward the southeast, to the outskirts of Northglade.
Group Naval attacks Northshore east of Northglade from the south, with seaborne drones.

relation.rel: attacks from the south, east of

lines.text: The battle plan's map draws two pale areas on a dark ground: a long inlet reaching down from the top, and an area along the lower right. Group Naval starts inside the lower one and Northglade sits at its edge; Groups North, Center and South start at the left and lower left, with dashed routes toward the right.

relation.b: two seas, Northglade on the southern coast

lines.text: The fiber-optic cables trailing behind the drones would stretch for hundreds of kilometers that night.
Telten, in Arctic core territory, is hundreds of kilometers further east than Northglade; seaborne drones land there and east of Northglade.
Fighting north, Group North reaches the river that marks the line between Veridian and core Arctic territory; Arctic towns lie nearby across it.
Thaldur is an island east of Northshore and core Arctic territory, too far away for either side to reach quickly.
On the mountain on Northglade's island, the peninsula dangling off the eastern end of Northshore, between there and Thaldur, is suggested as the place for a new Redshire.
Tens of thousands of people live on Thaldur, which has springs.
Glasscrown has a month and a half of polar night in winter.

relation.b: a month and a half of polar night

lines.text: A student argues that the United Cities stayed independent partly because their continent has so many mountains and peninsulas.
Each United City gives a share of the votes in its parliament to its neighbors.

The co-governance diagram links fifteen cities: Silverbeach–Mabuli, Silverbeach–Inglewore, Mabuli–Freetown, Inglewore–Hapton, Inglewore–Deplexi, Hapton–Imber, Hapton–Deplexi, Imber–Arturia, Imber–Deplexi, Arturia–Redshire, Arturia–Petersvil, Redshire–Petersvil, Redshire–Devanvil, Petersvil–Devanvil, Petersvil–Iptak, Deplexi–Freetown, Deplexi–Devanvil, Freetown–Devanvil, Freetown–Ondak, Devanvil–Ondak, Ondak–Iptak, Ondak–Mantak, Ondak–Belpaki, Iptak–Mantak, Iptak–Belpaki and Mantak–Belpaki.
Veridians call the cluster of Ondak, Iptak, Mantak and Belpaki "the aks".
Freetown is about as far from Redshire as you can get in the United Cities, except for Silverbeach and Mabuli.

relation.rel: nearly the farthest United City from

lines.text: In a Freetown conversation, someone says that about half the United Cities are closer to Redshire than Freetown is.
Arctic drones are flown around the northern United Cities, and patrol near Redshire.
The Arctics invaded Redshire by air and by land from the north, with vehicles coming out of underground tunnels.
Redshire has islands in the south, and its last garrison is in the south; that garrison's people are allowed to fly to Devanvil.
Redshire has castles, pine forests, large grasslands, red mountains with snowy tops, and a giant icy waterfall.

relation.b: castles, pine forests, grasslands, red snowy mountains

lines.text: From the Redshire coast, a seaborne drone heads west and lands its passengers on the coast of Arturia.
Freetown is building new roads and shelters, most on the northern side of town; a shelter is advertised "on the northern edge of central Freetown".

relation.rel: mostly on the northern side of

lines.text: From the highway out of Freetown's air harbor, Bai takes a nicer walled area in grey and purple for the local Greater Plum Harbor.
A Dzego council member predicts the Arctics would take Veridia, then the United Cities one by one, then "go south" to Messalia and Haragmir, leaving Dzego last.
In a Freetown conversation about the early United Cities, someone says the armies "of this continent" came together, which helped stop the Arctic offensive against Dzego.
